en: Litanies for Repentance:
Kneeling with both hands clasped, [the practitioner] should not allow the mind to be distracted or casual; with single-minded devotion, [one should focus intently].

However, if these light offenses are not ceased through sincere and earnest practice, even if one descends [to the lower realms], they will not be gathered or received; even if one petitions [the Buddhas], they will not appear. One must extinguish such offenses of negligence and arrogance; one must diligently apply oneself, contemplating them as if they were a cold disease treated by excellent medicine, so that one may attain recovery. Disciples such as I, [name], with single-minded devotion take refuge in all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, the Great Compassionate Fathers throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, who fill the entirety of space, who pity sentient beings and do not abandon their original vows or their compassion.
In this way, these Buddhas, throughout immeasurable and incalculable great kalpas, extensively practiced all difficult self-benefiting and other-benefiting ascetic practices;

for our sakes, they sacrificed their heads, eyes, marrow, brains, blood, flesh, limbs, kingdoms, cities, wives, children, elephants, horses, chariots, the seven treasures of gold and silver, clothing, food, drink, bedding, and medicine.
To all who come seeking, they give everything without any stinginess, giving rise to a heart of joy;
with courageous diligence, they practice the six perfections.
The perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and the power of aspiration;
and the profound, true Dharma of the twelve divisions of scripture.
Excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, and excellent in the end; its meaning is profound and its phrasing sublime.
It is pure, unadulterated, complete, and perfectly white, possessing the characteristics of the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
It is established by being retained within the same enlightened maintenance (*ekabodhādhiṣṭhāna*) as the pure realized wisdom of all Buddhas.
If there are sentient beings who receive and uphold even a single four-line verse,
it is superior to the giving of one's body and life as many times as the sands of the Ganges.

One fully cultivates and studies the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, great compassion, the three mindful establishments, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; all supernatural powers, all marks and signs of excellence, all merits, all wisdoms, and all myriad practices.
Having already perfected the merits and wisdom of the Three Vehicles, the Tripitaka, the untainted (anāsrava), the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta), the five kinds of pure eyes,

and the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), he has thereby attained unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), as well as the body of thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics, a vajra-like indestructible and firm body, the Dharma-body (dharmakāya), the eternal body, and the transformation body (nirmāṇakāya).
He delivers sentient beings from the three realms and the six paths of rebirth.
King of all sages, most honored and most noble in the heavens above and the earth below, there is none who can surpass him and none who can equal him.
He is called the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Great Compassionate Father.
He constantly employs skillful means and immeasurable kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity to deliver all suffering sentient beings,
enabling them to attain the eternal realm of peace and bliss that is nirvana.
If there are those who take refuge [in them], pay homage, make offerings, extol, and praise them;
or if they hear their names or behold their forms;
or if they burn incense, prostrate themselves, circumambulate, and perform the practice of walking meditation [before them].
The merit thus produced is immeasurable and boundless;
it exceeds Mount Sumeru and is deeper than the great ocean.
One regards all sentient beings with impartiality, as if they were one's only child.
Universally equal, they are free from love or hatred;
they act as the cause for transcendence for all sentient beings,
bestowing great kindness upon us and providing great benefit.
This is our true refuge, our true spiritual friend, and our true field of merit.
He is difficult to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas;
his praises cannot be fully exhausted even in hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.

Today we feel profound shame and remorse; we feel deep yearning and longing; we feel great joy; we feel deep affection and devotion; we feel profound veneration; we feel great celebration; and we feel deep reverence.

May the karmic obstructions possessed by these disciples be completely extinguished. [This concludes] one recitation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* (The Mother of All Buddhas), including its invocation and praise.
How could the merits within the bodies of all Buddhas ever be fully described?
The karmic obstacles inherent in this one life have already been extinguished.
I now prostrate and entreat you to accept my sincere repentance; standing before all Buddhas and sages, I deeply reproach myself and regret my transgressions.
They reformed their past ways and cultivated themselves for the future;
with utmost sincerity, they reached the point of baring their very livers and gallbladders,
feeling such piercing grief and sorrow that tears flowed down as they wept.
If one sincerely discloses and repents,
all light and heavy transgressions will be completely extinguished,
just as when clothing that has many stains and grease is washed clean.
If one wishes to wash them, they are placed in strong lye;
with a single wash, all grime and oiliness are completely removed.
Then, by rinsing them again with clear water, one obtains garments that are fresh and clean.
Repentance is also like this:
when one commits an offense and incurs sin, through repentance the sin is extinguished;
this is itself the body of pure merit.
Raising the body and kneeling with the right knee touching the ground—
do not let the left knee touch the ground—
place the palms together at the heart and give rise to a profound sense of longing and reverence.
We, the disciples [Name] and others,
together with all those present at this ritual site,
with one mind take refuge in all Buddhas and the assembly of Great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, filling the entirety of space and the void.

With great kindness and great compassion, may you take pity upon your disciples, gather and guide your disciples, never abandon your disciples, protect your disciples, rescue and deliver your disciples, liberate your disciples, save your disciples, provide for your disciples, benefit your disciples, lead your disciples forward, relieve your disciples, have compassion for your disciples, and accept your disciples.
I now repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions:
from beginningless time until this very day,
I have dwelt among ordinary beings, fully possessed of afflictions.
Enveloped by the immeasurable afflictions of greed, anger, and ignorance, their three karmas are overwhelmed and deluded; their three karmas are unwholesome.
They are characterized by greed, anger, jealousy, pride, arrogance, lack of benevolence, lack of righteousness, lack of reverence, and lack of veneration.
Toward their parents, they do not practice kindness or filial piety;
in speech and response, they glare askance and fix their eyes with anger,
causing resentment to arise and giving rise to suffering and distress.
They cause distress and confusion to their parents without realizing it;
or they lack reverence and obedience toward their brothers, sisters, and six kinds of relatives, failing to practice filial piety and righteousness;
or they act likewise toward their neighbors, friends, acquaintances, and those living in the four directions or next door.
They constantly encroach upon and deceive one another, constantly speak ill of one another, and constantly slander and revile one another.
Or they may misappropriate all the property of the Triple Gem,
or borrow things and fail to repay them.
It cannot repay the debt of even a single drop of water.
It cannot atone for the grave offenses of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes that lead to the Avīci Hell,
nor for the great false views that deny the existence of causes and effects.
They destroy stupas and ruin monasteries, burning sutras and images;
they slander the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, claiming it was not spoken by the Buddha;
they create obstacles and difficulties, and treat those above and below with contempt.
Whether large or small, they strike and revile others for both public and private matters;
they create various karmic obstacles by violating the fast and breaking the precepts;
they insult and humiliate their teachers and monks, and slander and deride the worthy and holy ones.
They treat monastics and laypeople with contempt through the three types of bodily action, the four types of verbal action, and the three types of mental action;
they engage in unwholesome conduct of the body,
such as killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.
With the mouth, one commits unwholesome actions such as false speech, frivolous talk, divisive speech,
and harsh abuse; with the mind,
one commits unwholesome actions such as covetousness, malice, and wrong views.
Constantly at night they perpetually committed the ten unwholesome karmas;
their various sinful obstructions were immeasurable and boundless.
Or, while irrigating their fields in their gardens and estates, they...
They harm and kill insects and ants, and they seek to exterminate mosquitoes and gadflies;
they injure lice and nits.
Regarding the giving of wealth and the giving of Dharma, they are constantly characterized by stinginess and parsimony.
They do not provide for what is needed;
seeing others in suffering, they are unable to rescue them,
nor do they give rise to compassion or loving-kindness.
Instead, they feel joy and satisfaction;
seeing their younger brother at ease, they do not rejoice in his excellence that surpasses their own,
even going so far as to act with jealousy and an intolerant mind.
Lacking compassion, pity, shame, and remorse,
their hearts harbored cruelty like that of tigers and wolves;
they frequented monasteries like rākṣasas.
They trample through mud and filth, drinking alcohol and eating meat without satiety or restraint;
they consume the five pungent roots and eat garlic and onions, polluting both the ordinary and the holy with their foul stench;
or they act with greed in the marketplace, seeking profit by force.
Using various expedients such as light scales and small measures, they plunder sentient beings and harm honest people;
they seek and demand much through evil means, seizing others' wealth and property without any self-awareness.
Through immeasurable killing, one severs great compassion;
through immeasurable stealing, one abandons human wealth and treasures;
through immeasurable sexual misconduct, one defiles pure celibacy.
False speech is immeasurable in its deception of all beings;
covetousness is immeasurable in its lack of satiety in the mind;
and divisive speech is immeasurable in its disruption of harmonious relations.
With immeasurable harsh speech, they reviled both ordinary beings and sages;
with immeasurable frivolous speech, they delighted in mocking the True Dharma;
with immeasurable anger, they beat and scolded sentient beings.
They have extensively committed immeasurable and boundless transgressions;
yet they see others practicing various wholesome deeds,
traveling between monasteries to pay homage to the Triple Gem.
They observe the fasts and precepts, recite and chant the sutras,
give rise to the bodhicitta, practice the bodhisattva path,
sit in meditation to cultivate the Way, and perform all manner of meritorious deeds.
They were unable to assist one another, nor could they rejoice in one another's merit;
they were unable to exhort or praise one another,
but instead created obstacles and gave rise to slander and derision.
Furthermore, they mock and deceive one another, destroying the causes for transcending the world that sentient beings cultivate;
they cause practitioners to harm sentient beings, become a thorn in the eyes of humans and devas, and retreat from the bodhicitta.
They act as great enemies and evil associates;
leading one another along the path, they fall into the three evil realms,
where they undergo the sufferings of hell for immeasurable kalpas.
Even if they emerge from hell and obtain a human body,
they will be blind, deaf, mute, or otherwise deficient in their faculties;
or they may be born in remote regions where the Buddha-dharma does not exist.
Ignorant of ritual and righteousness, and unable to distinguish between good and evil,
they live together with beasts and are born into families of false views;
they extensively commit all manner of transgressions and consequently fall back into the hells.
For immeasurable great kalpas it has been difficult to attain liberation.

Therefore, today, before the Buddhas of the ten directions, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, the assembly of great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, Arhats, and the noble Saṃgha; before Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, the eight classes of dragon-gods, the spirits of the underworld, the deities of the paths of karma, all numinous beings, and the various worthy sages who possess the supernormal powers of far-reaching vision with the divine eye, far-reaching hearing with the divine ear, and far-reaching knowledge of others' minds: [I now confess].

I testify that today, at this very moment, my disciple has conceived a profound sense of dread, a profound sense of weary detachment, a profound self-awakening, a profound sense of repentance, a profound sense of self-reproach, and a profound sense of shame; he does not dare to conceal [his faults].
From this day forward, I shall reform my dwelling and cultivate myself hereafter, never again daring to commit any sinful obstructions, whether many or few, light or heavy.
This very day, at this very moment, within a single thought, may all sinful obstructions be entirely extinguished.
I only pray that the Great Compassionate Honored Ones of the ten directions will bear witness, protect, and keep me in mind.
I now repent and shall not create [such karma] again.
May I and all sentient beings swiftly attain the eradication [of these offenses].
One should further contemplate that the nature of such offenses— the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes,
the four grave transgressions, the inverted slander and defamation of the Triple Gem,
and the sins of an icchantika— has arisen solely from a false and deluded mind.
There is nothing truly existent that can be apprehended; from the beginning, it is solely empty and quiescent.
May I and all sentient beings swiftly reach the fundamental nature of the mind and eternally extinguish the roots of transgression.
Having completed this repentance, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
